review_notes: Read the whole target file (134 lines) and inspected the relevant Mathlib sources: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean (Module.Basis.baseChange, baseChange_apply, baseChange_repr_tmul, Module.Free.tensor), Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Free.lean (equivFinsuppOfBasis), Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/FreeModule/Basic.lean (Module.Free.self), Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Charpoly/BaseChange.lean, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Trace.lean, Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Polynomial.lean and Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/IsBaseChangeFree.lean. I also checked that Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Basis is in scope here through Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.ToLin -> Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Projective -> Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Basis. Lean was not executed: the claim that `basis A b` and `b.baseChange A` are equal follows from the two files' `@[simp]` basis-vector lemmas (`1 ⊗ₜ b i`) plus `Basis.ext`, but this equality was not kernel-checked during review. Remaining uncertainty concerns the `AddCommGroup` restriction of `equivFinsuppOfBasis` versus `AddCommMonoid` here, and whether removing `instFree` would change typeclass-search behaviour in downstream files; neither was tested.

findings.excerpt:
variable (A) in
/-- Given an `R`-algebra `A`, this is the `A`-basis of `A ⊗[R] M` induced by an `R`-basis of `M`. -/
noncomputable def basis : Basis ι A (A ⊗[R] M) where
  repr := { basisAux A b with map_smul' := basisAux_map_smul b }
findings.problem: This is a second construction of exactly the same basis as `Module.Basis.baseChange` in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean:61–64. Both take `b : Basis ι R M` under the same assumptions (`[CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]`) and return `Basis ι A (A ⊗[R] M)`; both have the same basis vectors, since `basis_apply` (line 78) and `baseChange_apply` (Basis.lean:71–74) are the same `@[simp]` statement `_ i = 1 ⊗ₜ b i`, so the two bases are provably equal. Nevertheless every lemma here (`basis_repr_tmul`, `basis_repr_symm_apply`, `basis_repr_symm_apply'`, `basis_apply`, and the root-namespace `Module.Basis.baseChange_linearMap`/`baseChange_end`, plus `LinearMap.toMatrix_baseChange`) is stated only about the local `basis`, while `baseChange_repr_tmul` and `baseChange_apply` do not syntactically match `basis A b`. Concrete costs are visible downstream: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Charpoly/BaseChange.lean:27–28 uses `b.baseChange A` in exactly the same R-module-only setting and re-proves the matrix identity that `toMatrix_baseChange` states; Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Trace.lean:381–382 uses `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis`; Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Polynomial.lean:169–171 uses `basis A b₁` for `toMatrix_baseChange`. The root-namespace names `Module.Basis.baseChange_linearMap` and `Module.Basis.baseChange_end` are also misleading, since they are not about `Module.Basis.baseChange` at all.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the useful name as an abbreviation of the existing basis: define `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis A b := b.baseChange A` (or deprecate it in favour of `Module.Basis.baseChange`), delete `basisAux`, `basisAux_tmul` and `basisAux_map_smul`, and restate the `simp` lemmas here via `Module.Basis.baseChange_apply` and `baseChange_repr_tmul`. The `baseChange_linearMap`, `baseChange_end` and `toMatrix_baseChange` lemmas should then be stated for `b.baseChange A`, or moved next to `Module.Basis.baseChange` in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean. `instFree` can then use `Module.Free.of_basis (b.baseChange A)`.
findings.benefit: There would be one base-change basis and one `simp` set, so all of these lemmas apply uniformly whether a user writes `basis A b` or `b.baseChange A`; downstream files such as Trace.lean and Charpoly/BaseChange.lean could share the same `toMatrix` result instead of carrying two parallel APIs and conversions.

/-- The lift of an `R`-basis of `M` to an `S`-basis of the base change `S ⊗[R] M`. -/
noncomputable
def baseChange (b : Basis ι R M) : Basis ι S (S ⊗[R] M) :=
  (tensorProduct (.singleton Unit S) b).reindex (Equiv.punitProd ι)

@[simp]
lemma baseChange_apply (b : Basis ι R M) (i) :
    b.baseChange S i = 1 ⊗ₜ b i := by
  simp [baseChange, tensorProduct]

@[simp]
theorem basis_apply (i : ι) : basis A b i = 1 ⊗ₜ b i := basis_repr_symm_apply b 1 i

findings.excerpt:
variable (A) in
/-- Given an `R`-algebra `A` and an `R`-basis of `M`, this is an `R`-linear isomorphism
`A ⊗[R] M ≃ (ι →₀ A)` (which is in fact `A`-linear). -/
noncomputable def basisAux : A ⊗[R] M ≃ₗ[R] ι →₀ A :=
  _root_.TensorProduct.congr (Finsupp.uniqueLinearEquiv R A ()).symm b.repr ≪≫ₗ
    (finsuppTensorFinsupp R R A R PUnit ι).trans
      (Finsupp.lcongr (Equiv.uniqueProd ι PUnit) (_root_.TensorProduct.rid R A))
findings.problem: `basisAux` is the coordinate isomorphism `A ⊗[R] M ≃ ι →₀ A` built from `b.repr`. Mathlib already has the same coordinate isomorphism, with the stronger scalar structure, as `Algebra.TensorProduct.equivFinsuppOfBasis : (A ⊗[R] V) ≃ₗ[A] (ι →₀ A)` in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Free.lean:41–45. The docstring here explicitly says the map "is in fact `A`-linear", and `basisAux_map_smul` (lines 58–61) exists only to add that `A`-linearity by hand. `basisAux` is public but is used only to build `basis` (line 66) and `basis_repr_tmul` (line 71), so this file exposes a second public coordinate equivalence with a different scalar ring and different additivity hypotheses, and there is no lemma relating it to `equivFinsuppOfBasis`. A user seeking the base-change coordinate equivalence therefore has to choose between two unrelated names and cannot directly use the existing `A`-linear API.
findings.proposed_change: If `basis` is redefined via `b.baseChange A`, delete `basisAux`, `basisAux_tmul` and `basisAux_map_smul` entirely. If an explicit R-linear coordinate equivalence is still wanted, derive it from `(b.baseChange A).repr` or from `Algebra.TensorProduct.equivFinsuppOfBasis` (where `[AddCommGroup M]` holds) rather than introducing another definition.
findings.benefit: Removes a public implementation detail and a duplicated coordinate isomorphism; `A`-linearity comes from the existing `LinearEquiv A` rather than from a bespoke `basisAux_map_smul` lemma. Users find one coordinate-equivalence API instead of two incompatible ones.

/--
The `A`-algebra isomorphism `A ⊗[R] V ≃ₗ[A] (ι →₀ A)` coming from an
`ι`-indexed basis of a free `R`-module `V`.
-/
@[simps! apply symm_apply]
noncomputable def Algebra.TensorProduct.equivFinsuppOfBasis :
    (A ⊗[R] V) ≃ₗ[A] (ι →₀ A) :=
  open scoped Classical in
  (b.repr.baseChange R A _ _) ≪≫ₗ TensorProduct.finsuppScalarRight R A A ι
theorem basisAux_map_smul (a : A) (x : A ⊗[R] M) : basisAux A b (a • x) = a • basisAux A b x :=

findings.excerpt:
instance instFree (R A M : Type*)
    [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module.Free R M]
    [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A] :
    Module.Free A (A ⊗[R] M) :=
  Module.Free.of_basis <| Algebra.TensorProduct.basis A (Module.Free.chooseBasis R M)
findings.problem: The statement `Module.Free A (A ⊗[R] M)` is already supplied by the generic instance `Module.Free.tensor` in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean:196–199, specialized to `S := A`, first module `A` and second module `M`: it requires `Module.Free A A` (provided by `Module.Free.self`, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/FreeModule/Basic.lean:156–157) and the given `Module.Free R M`. Thus this file registers a second instance for the same class and type, whose proof additionally goes through the duplicate `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis` from the first finding. The concrete costs are two independent instance-resolution paths for the same fact, and a file-level dependency of freeness on the duplicate basis; the module docstring also advertises `instFree` as new main API even though the generic tensor-product instance already gives it.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the declaration if a specialized instance is desired, but prove it from the existing generic instance, e.g. by specializing `Module.Free.tensor` (with `Module.Free.self`), so that it no longer depends on `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis`; alternatively remove the instance and rely on `Module.Free.tensor` in downstream files. Update the main-declarations documentation accordingly.
findings.benefit: A single instance path for base-change freeness, and `instFree` no longer forces this file to retain the duplicated basis API. Downstream users get the fact from the general tensor-product instance and can remove the extra dependency on Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/Free.lean.
